cases.description: When the ExecutionConfig reports failFast = true, the validator should not report child errors (method returns false).
When the ExecutionConfig reports failFast = false, the validator should aggregate child errors (method returns true).
Passing a null ExecutionContext should result in a NullPointerException because the method dereferences the argument.
When ExecutionContext.getExecutionConfig() returns null, the method dereferences the result and throws a NullPointerException.
If ExecutionConfig.isFailFast() throws a RuntimeException, the exception should propagate out of reportChildErrors.
ExecutionConfig.isFailFast() returns true and increments a counter as a side‑effect; reportChildErrors should return false and the side‑effect should be observed exactly once.
ExecutionConfig.isFailFast() returns false and increments a counter as a side‑effect; reportChildErrors should return true and the side‑effect should be observed exactly once.
Using a spy for ExecutionContext and ExecutionConfig where isFailFast() returns true; verify that getExecutionConfig() and isFailFast() are each invoked exactly once and the method returns false.
Using a spy for ExecutionContext and ExecutionConfig where isFailFast() returns false; verify that getExecutionConfig() and isFailFast() are each invoked exactly once and the method returns true.
Call reportChildErrors twice with the same ExecutionContext where failFast = true; both invocations should consistently return false.
Call reportChildErrors twice with the same ExecutionContext where failFast = false; both invocations should consistently return true.
ExecutionContext.getExecutionConfig() throws IllegalStateException; the exception should propagate out of reportChildErrors.
ExecutionConfig.isFailFast() throws an AssertionError (an Error); the method should not catch it and the AssertionError should propagate.
